title: SG-5 · Implement round lifecycle and admin API
summary: Round state machine, snapshot freeze, scheduler and token-protected admin API in the Go backend
description: Context: the backend stores contributions as Markdown under worlds/<world>/rounds/<round>/contributions and has no round write model, scheduler or admin API. Desired behavior: a round model persisted in round.yaml with a transition table, open/close that freeze a snapshot.yaml and record the Git commit SHA, a clock-injected scheduler, and admin endpoints behind an admin token. Expected result: rounds move through the lifecycle only by legal transitions and admins can drive them over HTTP. Why: the Worker and the next-round cycle depend on a trustworthy round record.
acceptance_criteria: Given a round in any status, when a transition not in the table is requested, then it is rejected with ErrIllegalTransition and round.yaml is unchanged
Given an OPEN round, when it is closed, then snapshot.yaml is written once, the freeze commit SHA is recorded and status is CLOSED
Given a frozen round, when a contribution is saved, then the store rejects it and no file is written
Given a fake clock, when it passes starts_at or ends_at, then the scheduler opens or closes the round
Given a request without or with a wrong admin token, when any admin endpoint is called, then the response is 401

in_scope: admin middleware, round endpoints, execution endpoints
config for admin token and round defaults
out_of_scope: changing the existing world current-round reader

technical_constraints: No database; state lives in YAML files committed through gitrepo.Committer
Go 1.22, chi v5, yaml.v3, module github.com/worldseed/storyforge/backend
Clock is injected, never time.Now directly in tested code
definition_of_done: All six requirements implemented with unit tests passing via go test ./...
non_functional: Admin token compared in constant time
